clue.text: Helpful maxim, not in favour of mood changer

parts.note: auxiliary means giving help or support

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the following piece from the maxim's synonym

parts.note: a proverb is a pithy saying or maxim
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A wise saying, opposed to something that alters one's temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mood' is the grammatical term (indicative, subjunctive) rather than a feeling; words like 'might' or 'would' shift a verb's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Helper words such as 'may' or 'would' alter the grammatical mood of the main verb they accompany.

clue.text: What church supporter did in care home?

definitions.meaning: a curate helps a vicar run a benefice, which the Church calls a living, so he helped that living
a residential setting where elderly people get support with daily life

explanation.surface: A question about what a churchgoing helper did while in a residential home.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' is a Church of England benefice, the post and income of a parish priest; a curate assists in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported housing for elderly residents, giving help with everyday tasks, is what a residential care facility provides.

clue.text: Periodically, 54 times nothing mounts up

parts.note: the multiplication sign looks like the letter X

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: none means nothing

explanation.surface: Every so often, fifty-four lots of zero somehow accumulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it belongs to the definition: element 54 in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas has atomic number fifty-four, its place in the periodic table of the elements.

clue.text: Key point one found in pub relating to supply of men

indicators.note: found in says the following pieces sit inside the pub word

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
the gist is the main or key point
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The central argument was discovered in a bar, concerning how troops are provisioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Military logistics is the organisation of moving, supplying and quartering troops, so the adjective concerns provisioning soldiers.

clue.text: Claiming a belt fits around most of gut

indicators.note: fits around says the belt word is placed around the shortened gut

parts.note: a ring is a band or belt encircling something

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Asserting that a waistband goes round nearly all of one's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GUT to GU.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguing that something is so means asserting or maintaining it, as in 'he argued he was innocent'.

clue.text: Surrender the result of cows producing more?

definitions.meaning: to give up or hand over

definitions.text: the result of cows producing more?
definitions.meaning: a herd's milk yield going higher, read whimsically as a phrase

explanation.surface: Capitulate: what happens when dairy herds give extra milk?
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish or give something over, such as a secret or a fortress, is to hand it across.

clue.text: Style displayed in cycling lane

indicators.note: cycling means a letter is moved round from one end of the word to the other

explanation.surface: Flair on show while riding a bike in a road lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final E of LANE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair or dash, a stylish verve, is the French-derived sense used in English.

clue.text: Something Bob the Builder might do in two different books involving twist

definitions.text: Something Bob the Builder might do

indicators.note: involving means the books wrap around the twist word

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book, and a work is also a book
to rick is to wrench or twist a joint

explanation.surface: A cartoon builder's activity, described as two volumes enclosing a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob the Builder is a British children's TV character, a cheerful builder.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying bricks into walls is the kind of construction job a children's cartoon builder carries out.

clue.text: Any character involved in direct payment authorisation?

parts.note: any character of the alphabet is a letter
of can mean in, as in 'made of wood' meaning made in wood

indicators.note: involved means the letters of direct are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Is any symbol mixed up in authorising a straight payment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges DIRECT into CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank document guaranteeing a buyer's payment to a seller authorises settlement of a trade.

clue.text: Misbehave excitedly in audition in place of worship

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to misbehave is to sin, and a-go-go means excitedly or in lively fashion, so sin a-go-go

explanation.surface: Behaving badly with wild enthusiasm at a tryout held in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout, but here means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish house of prayer is a building for religious services.

clue.text: Compound starts to affect me, infecting nerve endings

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the next three words
endings means the two letters at either end of nerve

explanation.surface: A chemical begins to have an effect on me, invading my nerve terminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endings' takes both ends of 'nerve', N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic chemical derived from ammonia is a compound in chemistry.

clue.text: Cavity appears in useless bottles

indicators.note: bottles means the words hold the entry inside them, running across the gaps

explanation.surface: A hollow turns up in empty flasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun for containers but is a verb: the words keep the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-filled hollow in the skull bones near the nose is a bodily cavity.

clue.text: Motor race among leaders of drivers yesterday

parts.note: in means among, as in 'in the crowd'

indicators.note: leaders of means take the front letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A car race featured with yesterday's top drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy 500 is the famous race at Indianapolis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indianapolis 500 is a celebrated American car race, known by its short name.

clue.text: Heartlessly ruined sketch

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, financially ruined

explanation.surface: A cruelly spoiled comic drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes N, the middle letter of SKINT, which is British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic performance or sketch is a brief humorous piece.

clue.text: Goes in search of fashionable holiday boat

parts.note: to cruise is to go about looking for something, such as custom or a partner
hip means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone seeks out a trendy vessel for a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger liner taking tourists on leisure voyages is a vessel for a vacation.

clue.text: Newton's overwhelmed by genius somehow succeeding

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the unit sits surrounded by the rearranged word
somehow says the letters of genius are arranged in some other way

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force, with 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton is outclassed by a mind of genius, achieving success somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal follows its fodder, GENIUS, which is rearranged around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing means following on afterwards, as succeeding events come next in turn.

clue.text: Balanced my crimes out over time

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters cover and enclose the next piece
out means the letters of the words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone even-handed has worked off their misdeeds over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MY CRIMES into SYMMERIC, which goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape whose halves mirror each other is evenly proportioned on both sides.

clue.text: Dangerous to change sides in supper to make room

indicators.note: the outer letters of supper are S and R, so one swaps for the other

parts.note: parlous means perilous or dangerous

explanation.surface: A risky business, switching seats at dinner to create space.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sides' of 'supper' are its end letters S and R; the final S of PARLOUS becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room or front room in an old house was a reception chamber.

clue.text: Beat a touch upset in dance

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: upset means the following pieces are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: to dab is to touch lightly

explanation.surface: A rhythm, slightly off, during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A DAB round into BADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian partner dance with fast hip movements was a craze around 1990.

clue.text: April Fools' Day or beginning of idiocy from first principles

parts.note: the first of April, written as Apr and the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A prank day or the onset of foolishness, reasoning from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'from what comes before', it describes reasoning from theory rather than experience.

clue.text: Consider old folio trailing poor Yorick's finale

indicators.note: trailing means the old folio pieces come behind what precedes them

parts.note: thin means poor or meagre

indicators.note: finale means the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Ponder an old Shakespeare folio that follows Yorick's sorry end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Hamlet: Shakespeare's plays were printed in the First Folio, and Yorick is the dead jester whose skull Hamlet holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something to mind or contemplate it is to ponder it.

clue.text: American sweet almost made a hole round fabric

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taffy is the American name for toffee

indicators.note: round means the word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: acid ate into metal: to eat is to wear a hole

explanation.surface: An American candy almost burned a hole around some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Acid that 'ate' through metal made a hole in it, hence the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp, lustrous silk or synthetic cloth used for ballgowns is a textile.

clue.text: Struggle with expectation

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Wrestling with what one anticipates.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something in view means having it as an aim or anticipated prospect.

clue.text: Count half of wall drawings

indicators.note: half of means only the opening half of the word's letters is kept

parts.note: graffiti are drawings or writing scrawled on walls

explanation.surface: Tally up half the pictures sprayed on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' is the noun, a nobleman, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German title for an earl or count.

clue.text: Burning coal ends in climate doom, bishop fears occasionally

indicators.note: ends in means take the final letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Fossil fuel burning may spell climate disaster, a bishop sometimes worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'fears', E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a dying fire is a smouldering piece of coal.

clue.text: Revolutionised India with box containing hot appetiser

indicators.note: revolutionised means the whole sequence is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: containing means the box word holds the hot letter

parts.note: to jab is to punch, as in boxing

explanation.surface: India transformed, with a sparring match involving spicy food.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus JAHB reads IJAHB, which 'Revolutionised' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-fried Indian vegetable fritter, often onion, is served as a starter.

clue.text: Rodent catcher spends little time for employer

indicators.note: spends means the following piece is used up, so it goes

parts.note: a mouser is a cat good at catching mice
mo is a short moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A cat that hunts mice uses up a moment for its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' means one who employs something, a user, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a tool or service puts it to work, making use of it.

clue.text: Lousy rental returns housing Welsh girl

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
housing says the two words keep the letters held inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shoddy let comes back accommodating a young woman from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'housing' in the definition, but it is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'Welsh girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a typically Welsh female first name, well known from the sitcom Gavin and Stacey.

clue.text: Picked up about firm taking on third of executives

parts.note: over can mean about, as in 'talk it over'

indicators.note: taking on means the firm word takes in the next letter

parts.note: hard means firm or solid

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Collected regarding a company recruiting a third of its directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something by chance, eavesdropping on a remark, is catching it.

clue.text: Criminal trap con laid in one of four ways

indicators.note: criminal means the letters are treated wrongly, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker's snare set by a fraudster in one direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the four main compass directions.
